headline: On the hottest day of the summer, walkers on 72% of Milton Keynes' footpaths faced very strong heat stress.
deck: That is a feels-like temperature of 38 °C or more, for at least an hour.
sources:
The shape. Environment Agency lidar flown in the winters of 2019–20 and 2020–21 gives the shape of the area; a custom deep-learning model sorts its points into ground, buildings, trees and water.

The heat. SOLWEIG (Lindberg et al. 2008) follows the sun over them hour by hour on 13 August 2026 and, with the Met Office's 2 km UKV air temperature, humidity and wind, gives the feels-like temperature (UTCI) on each 1 m square. From a UTCI of 38 °C (very strong heat stress), a walker's core temperature starts to rise within half an hour (Błażejczyk et al. 2013).

Paths, stops and plans. Footpaths are from OpenStreetMap, bus stops from NaPTAN; places built since the flight are greyed. New trees are placed as TreePlanter does (Wallenberg et al. 2022). Urban means the census areas the ONS classes as urban (2021).

urban.headline: On the hottest day of the summer, walkers on 71% of Milton Keynes' footpaths faced very strong heat stress.

stops.name: stops

urban.headline: 656 trees and 36 shelters would spare people waiting at all 1,143 bus stops from very strong heat stress.
urban.deck: As it was, 447 of them reached 38 °C.
urban.note: 656 new trees, the fewest that shade every stop in each hour it would reach 38 °C, and a shelter at the 36 stops no tree can shade. Each is 9.8 m tall, the median of the trees beside paths and stops now.

stops.label: Shade at bus stops
stops.headline: 741 trees and 53 shelters would spare people waiting at all 1,281 bus stops from very strong heat stress.
stops.deck: As it was, 499 of them reached 38 °C.
stops.note: 741 new trees, the fewest that shade every stop in each hour it would reach 38 °C, and a shelter at the 53 stops no tree can shade. Each is 9.8 m tall, the median of the trees beside paths and stops now.

trees.name: trees

urban.headline: 10% more trees would cut the footpaths where walkers face very strong heat stress, from 71% to 45%.
urban.deck: Every bus stop would stay below 38 °C too, with a shelter at each of the 28 that no tree can shade.

trees.label: 10% more trees
trees.headline: 10% more trees would cut the footpaths where walkers face very strong heat stress, from 72% to 47%.
trees.deck: Every bus stop would stay below 38 °C too, with a shelter at each of the 44 that no tree can shade.
trees.note: 88,753 new trees, one for every 10 standing now: first by the bus stops, then where they shade the most sunlit footpaths in the hottest hours. Each is 9.8 m tall, the median of the trees beside paths and stops now.
